# Rome2Rio

> Rome2Rio is a global trip planning search engine covering flights, trains, buses, ferries, driving, and more across 160+ countries. Our goal is to show travellers every way to get from A to B — with prices, timetables, and booking options from thousands of operators — in a single search.

## How the site works

Rome2Rio is a **search and discovery product**. Users search for routes, explore options, and are directed to operator or OTA booking pages to complete their purchase. There is no checkout flow on Rome2Rio itself. However, users can create a free account to save searches, access personalised recommendations, and manage preferences.

## Core page types

### 1. Search results pages (route pages)

The heart of the product. Each page covers a specific origin–destination pair and shows all travel modes (flight, train, bus, ferry, drive, etc.) with indicative prices, durations, and operator names. These pages are generated for millions of O&D pairs globally.

Top examples:
- [London to Paris](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/London/Paris)
- [Sydney to Melbourne](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Sydney/Melbourne)
- [New York to Boston](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/New-York/Boston)
- [Bangkok to Chiang Mai](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Bangkok/Chiang-Mai)
- [Barcelona to Rome](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Barcelona/Rome)
- [Amsterdam to Berlin](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Amsterdam/Berlin)
- [Tokyo to Osaka](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Tokyo/Osaka)
- [Cape Town to Johannesburg](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Cape-Town/Johannesburg)

### 2. Place / destination pages

Overview pages for individual cities, airports, train stations, and regions. These summarise how to get to and from a place, what transport hubs serve it, and link to popular onward routes.

Top examples:
- [London](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/London)
- [Paris](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Paris)
- [New York](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/New-York)
- [Tokyo](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Tokyo)
- [Sydney](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Sydney)

### 3. Transport mode pages

Dedicated pages explaining a specific transport mode available between two places — for example, the train options between two cities, or bus services on a corridor. These go deeper than the search results page, with more operator detail, schedules, and booking guidance.

Examples:
- [Train from London to Edinburgh](https://www.rome2rio.com/train/London/Edinburgh)
- [Bus from London to Manchester](https://www.rome2rio.com/bus/London/Manchester)

## Supporting content

### About Rome2Rio
General information about the company, mission, how the product works, and team.
- [How Rome2Rio works](https://www.rome2rio.com/blog/2025/12/02/how-to-use-rome2rio/)
- [About us](https://www.rome2rio.com/about)
- [Contact](https://help.rome2rio.com/en/support/tickets/new)
- [Press](https://www.rome2rio.com/media/)
- [Careers](https://www.rome2rio.com/careers/)

### Legal
- [Terms of use](https://www.rome2rio.com/terms-of-use/)
- [Privacy policy](https://www.rome2rio.com/privacy-policy/)

### Travel guides and editorial
Rome2Rio publishes travel guides to help users plan trips. These are informational articles about destinations, transport tips, and travel itineraries. They do not contain booking flows.

- [Travel guides](https://www.rome2rio.com/travel-guides/)

Example topics include: how to get around a country by train, the best ways to travel between major city pairs, visa and entry information for popular routes, seasonal travel tips.

### Blog
The Rome2Rio blog covers travel inspiration, product updates, and transport industry news.
- [Blog](https://www.rome2rio.com/blog)

### Help / FAQ
Support content covering common questions about how to use Rome2Rio, understanding search results, and what to do if information appears incorrect.
- [Help centre](https://help.rome2rio.com/)

## User account

Rome2Rio supports user accounts. There is no cart or checkout — all purchases happen on third-party operator or booking sites.

Logged-in users can save favourite routes, access recent searches, and personalise their experience.
